items.title: After Star Fox's Launch and Zelda: Ocarina of Time's Announcement, Miyamoto Defends Nintendo's Recent Spate of Remakes and Says They Lead to 'Future Developments'
items.description: Nintendo legend Shigeru Miyamoto has defended the company's remakes, and said that newer versions of classic titles can lead to "future developments" — something that fans are keen to see for Star Fox and Zelda.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Nintendo legend Shigeru Miyamoto has defended the company's remakes, and said that newer versions of classic titles can lead to "future developments" — something that fans are keen to see for Star Fox and Zelda.

While Nintendo remaking and re-releasing its classic games is absolutely nothing new, it's fair to point out that two of the company's biggest Switch 2 games this year will be very familiar to long-term fans. Star Fox, which launched last month, sparked conversation online for technically being the company's third reimaging of its N64 classic. The upcoming Switch 2 incarnation of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, meanwhile, will follow various re-releases of the N64 original, as well as its 3DS port.

Now, speaking to Japanese gaming magazine Famitsu (via Nintendo Everything), Miyamoto has addressed the claim that there are too many Nintendo remakes — and hinted that the projects will subsequently serve as the basis for something new.

"Some people might say there are a lot of remakes, but after five years, a lot of people have outgrown games and stop playing them," Miyamoto said. "Young people today don't have the opportunity to play games from 10 years ago, so remaking them to be more playable and releasing them again is a good way to meet the demand.

"Letting people know the original games also leads to future developments," he teased, "so we've been actively pursuing that recently."

Following the appearance of Fox McCloud in this year's Super Mario Galaxy Movie, as well as the Switch 2's Star Fox remake, many fans expect an all-new Star Fox game to follow in due course. As for Zelda, it is inevitable that a full-blown follow-up to Tears of the Kingdom is in the works, while Ocarina of Time launches later this year to keep fans busy.

After a major leak and much fan speculation, Nintendo finally confirmed it was remaking Ocarina of Time during last month's major Nintendo Direct. An initial teaser revealed little, though showed the game's 3D art style and confirmed it will launch sometime later in 2026. However, a now-removed product description has hinted that the game will likely be a faithful remake.

Photo by Amy Sussman/Getty Images.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Sony Knew Killing Discs Would Be 'An Enormous PR Issue' and Had 'Strictest' Guidelines to Gag Staff From Commenting on Controversy, Former God of War Dev Claims
items.description: Sony knew its decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs would spark outrage, and reportedly issued staff with the "strictest" social media guidelines to stop them from publicly commenting on the controversy.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Sony knew its decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs would spark outrage, and reportedly issued staff with the "strictest" social media guidelines to stop them from publicly commenting on the controversy.

That's according to God of War Laufey writer Alanah Pearce, who alleged in a new YouTube video that the restrictions were the most stringent that PlayStation staff had seen — as Sony anticipated its announcement to cause significant blowback.

Earlier this month, Sony stunned fans by announcing that it would stop launching PlayStation 5 games on physical discs from January 2026 onwards. While the move follows a gradual shift in video game sales from boxed copies to digital downloads over the past decade, gamers who prefer to own a physical edition, or who are concerned by the impact this will have on game preservation, have been vocal in their opposition.

Sony's rationale for ditching discs is that it's simply following consumer trends. "In response to shifting trends in consumer preference, new games will be released on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only," Sid Shuman, Senior Director, Sony Interactive Entertainment Content Communications, said in a post on PlayStation Blog.

"As consumer preferences and the broader entertainment industry continue to shift away from physical discs to digital, physical game disc production for all new games releasing on PlayStation consoles will be discontinued starting January 2028. Following this date, new games will be available on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only. This transition has no impact on games that already released, or will be releasing, prior to January 2028 in disc format.

"This is a natural direction for Sony Interactive Entertainment to adapt to consumer trends as the general preference for digital media significantly outpaces physical discs. This transition will enable us to align more closely with how most of our community prefers to access and play games today."

Despite a high-profile petition and a constant stream of comments on Sony's subsequent livestreams and social media posts — even overshadowing the release of new games that have nothing to do with the controversy — there's been no sign that the PlayStation maker will change its mind. For now, Sony simply hasn't commented further — and is unlikely to do so, Pearce suggested.

"Sony already knew everyone would be pissed off," Pearce began. "They knew this. People working at PlayStation first-party studios told me that Sony had the strictest social media guidelines for this particular thing that they've ever seen issued.

"Sony does somewhat regularly tell employees what they can or can't say about certain things," she explained. "I was under a lot of guidelines when I was working on God of War Laufey. I still am, and they did send me guidelines regarding what I could say on the day that the game was announced. But in this instance, it is apparently the strictest the employees I spoke to have sever seen regarding public communications. They would only have done this if they knew it was going to be an enormous PR issue. This is no surprise to them."

For Sony, going all-digital for new game releases will earn it more money from every sale at a time when console sales are expected to plummet due to their rising costs. For a first-party PlayStation game such as The Last of Us, Sony will only keep around 65% of the money from a physical copy, with around 30% going to the retailer and roughly another 5% on manufacturing costs. Meanwhile, for a physical copy of a third-party game such as the Activision-published Call of Duty, Sony will get a licensing fee, likely around 15%. For digital sales, Sony keeps 100% of first-party game revenue, and a far better cut from third-party titles.

More than 335,000 people have now signed the Change.org petition calling on Sony to U-turn on its decision, though Pearce said that this would not prompt Sony to change its mind. Speaking to IGN, analysts have all said similar. Dr. Serkan Toto, CEO of Japanese game industry consultancy firm Kantan Games, suggested that even if half a million people cancelled their PlayStation Plus subscription in protest, it would be just a drop in the ocean for Sony.

"I sympathize with physical media fans, but Sony will not reverse this decision," Toto told IGN. "They of course knew what the online reaction would look like, and they now wait for this storm to pass.

"Sony has over 120 million active PlayStation users," he continued. "Around 50 million people subscribe to PlayStation Plus. As a thought experiment, let's say 500,000 cancel in protest, that would be just 1% of that business gone — of course not enough for Sony to start rethinking. Digital is just too lucrative."

Image credit: Jaap Arriens/NurPhoto via Getty Images.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: For One Night Only is a New Showcase Celebrating UK Video Game Talent, Here’s How To Watch.
items.author: George Forsyth-Nash
items.content:
The UK has a proud history of creating iconic video game franchises and is home to world-renowned developers ⁠– now, a new major showcase event, For One Night Only, is shining a light on the world-class games made by British studios.

Throughout its approximately 60-80 minute livestream, For One Night Only will feature new trailers, exclusive reveals and on-stage interviews with some of the UK’s biggest and best games industry talent. With a lineup that includes IO Interactive, Team 17 and Criterion (just to name a few), it's easy to see why the UK continues to be a games industry powerhouse.

How to Watch For One Night Only

Join in and celebrate the UK video game industry by watch For One Night Only on Wednesday, 29th July at 7PM BST / 11AM PST via the following platforms:

IGN

YouTube

Facebook

X

Twitch

Steam

What to Expect From For One Night Only

Hosted by comedian Bec Hill in front of a VIP industry audience at Outernet in London’s West End, For One Night Only will feature a mix of exclusive reveals, trailers and never-before-seen interviews from both industry titans and indie talent.

A selection of the developers and publishers, and the games they are showcasing include: Annapurna Interactive with The Lost Wild and Silent Hill: Townfall, Bandai Namco with Little Nightmares 3, IO Interactive with 007 First Light and Yogscast Games with PlateUp!.

For One Night Only will also be supported by a special Steam sale featuring participating British video game studios. The FONO Steam sale starts at 6PM BST on 29th July and runs for one week, so you can make a saving when jumping in to the games featured in the show!

Don’t miss the For One Night Only stream on Wednesday, 29th July at 7PM BST / 11AM PST. In the meantime catch any updates and additional information over on the official For One Night Only social media accounts:

TikTok: @ForOneNightOnlyGames

Insta: @ForOneNightOnlyGames

Twitch: @For_One_Night_Only_Games

Bluesky: @fonogames

YouTube: @ForOneNightOnlyGames

X: @FONO_Games

items.title: First Look at Warhammer Blood Bowl, the Free Overhaul for Blood Bowl 3 Due Out Fall 2026
items.description: Warhammer Blood Bowl hits the end zone this fall, and we've got first-look screenshots and confirmed platforms for launch.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Warhammer Blood Bowl hits the end zone this fall, and we've got first-look screenshots and confirmed platforms for launch.

The video game adaptation of Games Workshop’s Warhammer fantasy football tabletop game is now in the hands of Warhammer 40,000: Battlesector publisher Slitherine, which obtained the licence, publishing rights, and back catalog from the collapsing Nacon.

Now, Slitherine has re-announced Warhammer Blood Bowl with a batch of screenshots, below. It’s due out this fall across PC, Xbox, and PlayStation.

Slitherine said Warhammer Blood Bowl is “built upon the solid foundations of Blood Bowl 3,” with series developer Cyanide still in place. The game will also adopt the latest official tabletop ruleset, updated through September 2025 (also known as Third Season Edition). The roster expands with the Bretonnians and Khemri Tomb Kings.

"At Slitherine, we're strategy gamers first and foremost, and Blood Bowl has always been one of our favorite tabletop games," said Marco Alessandro Minoli, Director of Publishing at Slitherine.

"We're incredibly proud to welcome this iconic franchise into our portfolio and to be working alongside the talented team at Cyanide. Our goal with Warhammer Blood Bowl is simple: we want this to become the definitive Blood Bowl video game — not just at launch, but for years to come. Our vision is to support and expand it over time, turning it into a living, constantly evolving experience, just as we've successfully done with other Warhammer titles such as Warhammer 40,000: Battlesector and Warhammer 40,000: Gladius."

Helpfully, everyone who owns Blood Bowl 3 on PC and consoles will receive Warhammer Blood Bowl as a free upgrade, keeping all previously purchased teams and cosmetics. A playable demo is set for the end of the summer on PC. It includes Rumble Mode, a fast-paced, dynamic 7-player format designed for quicker matches.

Blood Bowl 3 has a 'mixed' user review rating on Steam, and it's fair to say the game failed to meet fan expectations when it launched in 2023. IGN's Blood Bowl 3 review returned a 5/10. We said: "Blood Bowl 3 is a sloppy, muddy, buggy rehash of a better game."

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power is Finally Introducing Galadriel's Husband Celeborn — And a Famous Face From Stranger Things is Playing Her 'Lover-Boy' Beau
items.description: Galadriel's husband Celeborn will finally be introduced in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, with new episodes set to debut Stranger Things' Jamie Campbell Bower as her "lover-boy" partner.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Galadriel's husband Celeborn will finally be introduced in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, with new episodes set to debut Stranger Things' Jamie Campbell Bower as her "lover-boy" partner.

Exactly how Celeborn will be introduced — and where he's supposed to have been for the past two seasons — remains under wraps. But Empire has confirmed that Celeborn will feature in the show's upcoming third season, and that the actor behind Stranger Things' Vecna will play Galadriel's fair-headed fellow.

As Tolkien fans will know, Galadriel and Celeborn were married during Middle-earth's First Age, long prior to the events of the Second Age, which The Rings of Power is adapting. In the show's first season, Galadriel mentions that her husband never returned from fighting Morgoth — with the implication being that she has not seen him since.

Until now, our only glimpses of Celeborn on screen come from a couple of cameo appearances in Peter Jackson's The Lord of the Rings trilogy. But not to worry if you can't really remember him — he has very little to do, with Galadriel herself very much the star.

"This idea of longing and yearning is so pervasive in Tolkien's relationship with [his wife] Edith for the time that they were apart," Bower said of Celeborn and Galadriel's relationship, which is inspired by the author's long absences from his own wife during youth and while fighting in the First World War. "I really feasted on that idea. Celeborn has had to find a way to survive whilst longing for something that he so dearly loved and so dearly missed as well."

Bower described his character's demeanour as a "lover-boy," while Galadriel actress Morfydd Clark noted that her elf alter ego was "kind of rude to him in the books."

"She's the queen!" Clark concluded. "But Jamie looks exactly like how I would imagine Celeborn. He's such an elf."

Rings of Power is set to debut its third season via Prime Video at some point before the end of 2026 — a two-year wait for fans since the show's last episode. But while it may have been a couple of years for fans, it will have been even longer for Rings of Power's characters — who'll after something of a time jump. While Season 2 ended with Galadriel and her elvish friends finally united and ready to fight the growing threat of Sauron, the series' third run will fast forward to the middle of the subsequent conflict.

"Jumping forward several years from the events of Season 2, Season 3 takes place at the height of the War of the Elves and Sauron," an official synopsis reads, "as the Dark Lord seeks to craft the One Ring that will give him the edge he needs to win the war and conquer all Middle-earth at last."

Earlier this year, it was reported that Rings of Power was still on-track to run for five seasons, with the $1 billion Prime Video show claimed to be still under the protection of Amazon boss Jeff Bezos' "magical halo" despite its huge costs.

Image credit: Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Xbox Gamers Slam Paramount After Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game Suffers Shock Delay on Their Console Just Hours Before Launch
items.description: Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game has suffered a shock delay on Xbox just hours before it was due to come out, sparking a backlash from fans.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game has suffered a shock delay on Xbox just hours before it was due to come out, sparking a backlash from fans.

The Paramount Games Studio-published fighting game, developed by Gameplay Group International, was due out today, July 23, across PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, PC via Steam, and Nintendo Switch.

But in a note to fans published just a few hours ago, Paramount said the Switch version will be available as the Standard Edition only, and crossplay with other platforms and language localization beyond English will not be available. “We are committed to bringing these features, along with upgrading to Deluxe Edition, to players as soon as possible and will keep you updated on our timeline and progress,” Paramount said.

But it’s an even worse situation for Xbox fans, who have seen the game in its entirety delayed to September 3 — a 6-week wait that sets Xbox players back significantly on the competitive front. Paramount failed to say exactly what the issue was, speaking in vague terms to say it was due to “unforeseen circumstances on a backend feature.”

“For the Xbox community, we are forced to delay the release,” Paramount said. “Due to unforeseen circumstances on a backend feature, we will now launch by September 3. Existing preorders will remain active and will not be canceled.

“Our priority is delivering the best possible experience on every platform and we are working tirelessly to make that happen. Thank you for your patience, understanding and continued support. We’re excited to get everyone into the fight as soon as possible. Tune in here for updates as we have them.”

As you’d expect, Xbox gamers have reacted negatively to the news, with many of the replies highly critical of Paramount.

“F**k your game!” replied one person. “Delaying your game HOURS before release on XBOX is horrible management. Zero excuses. You should’ve known this WELL IN ADVANCE. Keep your game, not buying it. Was looking forward to it so much as an Avatar TLA fan.”

“Delaying an anticipated game by a month and a half less than 24 hours before release is actually insane,” said another. “Do better, @ParamountGames.”

“All my Xbox homies should get a free deluxe upgrade because this here is some bs of the highest degree. Xbox friends, please get your refunds,” another said.

“Wtf do you mean ‘existing preorders will remain active and will not be canceled?’ Watch this ticket support go through,” one person said. “There's no reason to make such an announcement with less than 24 hours till release. That's ridiculous.”

“Damn.. not sure to get the game now,” another added. “I'd rather just wait another month then. It just hurts the experience for everyone if not all of the potential player base is there.”

“Unforeseen circumstances on a backend feature isn't good enough,” another person said. “Explain the situation, this is terrible comms guys and you know that.”

items.title: Pokémon Diamond and Pearl Leak Reveals More Than 100 Scrapped Designs, Including Unseen Creatures and Missing Evolutions
items.description: Pokémon Diamond and Pearl fans are celebrating the unofficial reveal of more than 100 previously-unseen designs, including early drafts of known creatures, numerous scrapped species, and cut evolutions.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Pokémon Diamond and Pearl fans are celebrating the unofficial reveal of more than 100 previously-unseen designs, including early drafts of known creatures, numerous scrapped species, and cut evolutions.

Evidence of a discarded Delibird and Kecleon evolutions, Stantler and Lapras pre-evolutions, plus what look like a baby Plusle and Minun are all briefly seen. Completely cut Pokémon include creatures based on a crane, crickets, snails, molluscs, goats, mice, a platypus, and a swordfish can also be seen, as well as plants such as beansprouts and clover. There's even different designs for the region's starter Pokémon, such as a foam-headed Water-type dog, and a Grass-type wolf.

The source of these designs is a long-lost documentary made by Pokémon developer Game Freak that has never previously been seen in public. Made for the game's own staff as a record of their work, the film was originally handed out to employees on DVDs, who were sworn to keeping it private.

Now, 20 years later, the documentary has finally been obtained, and painstakingly sifted through by a team of fans — with the best archive of the material found on Lewtwo. The full documentary itself can also now be seen on YouTube (for now) and more permanently via the Internet Archive.

Scrapped Delibird evolution pic.twitter.com/CyGP2thilM

— Centro LEAKS (@CentroLeaks) July 22, 2026

Scrapped Water Starter Pokémon pic.twitter.com/1OO5j0VD7B

— Centro LEAKS (@CentroLeaks) July 22, 2026

EVEN MORE NEVER BEFORE SEEN BETA POKÉMON pic.twitter.com/i8PXnoYwnl

— Centro LEAKS (@CentroLeaks) July 22, 2026

As you might expect, fan excitement around the documentary's contents is huge — thanks to fact that the film was made originally for Game Freak staff, and is completely unfiltered in the content it shows. Game Freak guards its Pokémon design process with enormous secrecy, and it's unlikely this documentary would even be made today.

For many fans, the creation of games such as Pokémon Diamond and Pearl is something to be explored and celebrated, as a part of gaming's history that they want to see preserved. Of course, there's natural interest in the many, many Pokémon designs that have been left on the cutting room floor, but also a peek behind the curtain at the series' development. The documentary includes almost an hour of footage shot within Game Freak's offices, showing employees alternately working and goofing around, and the process used to design the Sinnoh region — from sketches to paper maps to real-world models made using blocks.

With such enormous secrecy around the creation of new Pokémon games, chances to get a peek behind the curtain are few and far between. The only release of scrapped Pokémon details to rival this in recent years has been the infamous Pokémon Teraleak, which originated in an illegal hack of data from Game Freak's internal servers.

Even 20 years on, there's even clues to Pokémon that may feature in future. New Pokémon generations have regularly featured updated versions of previously-cut designs (and indeed, the documentary shows creatures that strongly resemble the finished looks of Rowlet and Sandygast, finally released years later). One particular design here catches the eye — a yellow Shellos. This is a creature fans expect to pop up in next year's Pokémon Winds and Waves for Switch 2, after mention of it in this year's Pokémon Pokopia.

Yellow Shellos pic.twitter.com/IiU8Dm8ZKm

— Centro LEAKS (@CentroLeaks) July 22, 2026

items.title: NASCAR 26 Release Date Confirmed, Features Dynamic Track Surfaces, AI DNFs
items.description: Improvements incoming as iRacing builds upon last year’s foundation.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
iRacing has confirmed the release date for its second stab at a standalone NASCAR game, following on from last year’s robust NASCAR 25. NASCAR 26 will be officially launched on September 18, 2026 (albeit following a three-day early access period for purchasers of the game’s higher-priced ‘Gold Edition’).

A new developer diary published today, featuring producer Matt Lewis and creative director Mike DeVault, discussed a number of additions and improvements to this year’s game.

NASCAR 26 will feature dynamic track surfaces, which will rubber in as race weekends progress. This evolution will open up new strategies as new racing lines become available.

The team has also addressed some bugbears present in NASCAR 25 around road course track limits, as well as the fact that opponents would never retire – even following major incidents. The development team has loosened some of the track restrictions to cut down on unrealistic penalties, and NASCAR 26 will feature AI DNFs.

“These quality of life improvements, right?” said Lewis. “Which are minor asks in the grand scheme of things, but just again showing that we’re listening to the community.”

NASCAR 26 will also feature the 10-round Chase, which will be available as a completely standalone mode.

“You go in, you set up the field that you want to compete against and you just run those last 10 races,” explained Lewis. “So that’s going to be an awesome feature as well.”

New gameplay footage of NASCAR 26 is expected to be published next week.

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

items.title: Matt Damon Almost Starred as Robin in Two Different Batman Movies
items.description: “I remember Chris O’Donnell already had the part, but they were haggling over money,” explains Damon.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
The Odyssey star Matt Damon has recounted a time back in the beginning of his career where he auditioned to play Robin in not one, but two different live-action Batman movie projects.

Speaking with host Josh Horowitz on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, Damon first discussed auditioning for the Robin role during Tim Burton’s time at the helm of the films.

“I remember that we didn’t have sides,” said Damon, referring to the short excerpts of scripts provided to actors to perform during auditions. “It wasn’t like you’re reading a scene with Batman. It was so secretive that it was, like, you’re reading this other scene from some other movie.”

Robin ultimately never appeared in either of the two Tim Burton Batman movies, but this initial audition actually wasn’t Damon’s only brush with The Boy Wonder.

“Then, subsequent to that, in ’93, I got screentested; I was one of the final three to play Robin in the George Clooney [and] Joel Schumacher Batman,” continued Damon.

“I remember Chris O’Donnell already had the part, but they were haggling over money. So the studio was flexing, basically, by flying in two other people to screen test, but they wanted Chris – but they just wanted him for a price.”

Damon clarified he knew O’Donnell at the time.

“I remember calling up and I was, like, ‘I’ll work for a quarter of what that dude’s working for,’” he laughed. “I was like, ‘I want the job!’ Yeah, I flew in and auditioned for Joel, but I think they always intended [the role to O’Donnell]. I remember seeing Chris while he was making that – we were friends back then – and they always intended to give it to Chris.”

While a role in a Batman film never eventuated for Damon, his collaborations with an esteemed Batman director, Christopher Nolan, keep coming – from Interstellar to Oppenheimer, and on to this year’s The Odyssey.

IGN’s review of The Odyssey called it a “must-watch cinematic experience.”

items.title: Doom Co-Creator John Romero to Headline Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show 2026
items.author: Tristan Ogilvie
items.content:
John Romero, the co-founder of id Software and co-creator of Doom, Quake, and Wolfenstein 3D, has been confirmed as the headline keynote speaker for this year's Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show, to be held in Bangkok this October. The industry veteran's planned keynote, to be titled "Why We Still Make Games", promises to "reflect on a lifetime of building games, overcoming setbacks, and navigating decades of industry change." And presumably, unsuccessful attempts at making people his bitch.

While Romero left the Doom development studio some three decades ago, he recently took to social media to express his support for all id Software staff affected by the layoffs earlier this month that came off the back of Xbox's significant restructuring process.

“I’m so sorry for everyone at id Software affected by these layoffs,” Romero tweeted.

“I know what it feels like to leave id while id goes on. It’s a strange and painful thing to step away from a place that holds so much of your work, friendships and history."

Romero's current studio, Romero Games, has suffered its own setbacks as part of Xbox's ongoing cuts, with the studio's unannounced shooter cancelled in 2025 reportedly due to Microsoft pulling its funding. So he should certainly have a few things to chat about at Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show.

Romero is the latest speaker confirmed for this year's event. He joins co-founders Nick Herman and Dennis Lenart from AdHoc Studio, the team behind 2025's critically acclaimed hit Dispatch, as well as Zhen Fang, VP and Head of International at Roblox, and Yoan Fanise, creative director and founder of indie developer DigixArt. More speakers are expected to be confirmed in the lead up to the show.

Last year's event featured keynotes from Ubisoft and Naughty Dog developers, as well as a particularly impassioned and memorable address from Dead Space co-creator Glen Schofield who declared that the games industry was "broken, beaten, and battered." Schofield officially retired from games development less than 12 months later.

This year's Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show will apparently be its biggest to date, with the public area expanding to four halls, bringing the total event space to 35,000 square metres (in case you're counting). Major publishers including Nintendo, Bandai Namco, Capcom, and Sega will all be present on the show floor, and there will once again be a sizeable space for indies to showcase the best of local development talent from Southeast Asia and beyond.

Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show 2026 is set to run from October 29 to November 1, 2026, at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center in Bangkok.

Tristan Ogilvie is a senior video producer at IGN's Sydney office.

items.title: 50/50 Director Jonathan Levine in Talks to Direct Tom Cruise Sequel Days of Thunder 2
items.description: Paramount prepares to drop the hammer on another high-speed Tom Cruise legacy sequel.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
Director Jonathan Levine (50/50, Warm Bodies) is reportedly in talks to helm the long-awaited follow up to 1990 racing action-drama Days of Thunder, according to The Hollywood Reporter. Star Tom Cruise is aboard to reprise his role as NASCAR driver and Daytona 500 champ Cole Trickle, and is producing alongside Jerry Bruckheimer. Bruckheimer produced the original Days of Thunder in partnership with Don Simpson, who died in 1996.

The Hollywood Reporter notes Days of Thunder 2 is intended to be Cruise’s next production.

No further details are available in terms of the planned story for the sequel, or how it picks up from the original, but a script has been written by screenwriter and author Will Staples. Staples wrote the game Call of Duty 3: Modern Warfare alongside Paul Haggis (Million Dollar Baby, Crash) and Michael B. Jordan’s Without Remorse alongside Taylor Sheridan (Sicario, Yellowstone). His association with Cruise may date back to a rewrite of Mission: Impossible – Rogue Nation he was hired to tackle in 2014.

Days of Thunder is a fondly-remembered racing classic, which reteamed Cruise with late director Tony Scott following their work together on 1986’s Top Gun. Its stacked cast includes the late Robert Duvall, as well as Nicole Kidman, Michael Rooker, John C. Reilly, Cary Elwes, and Randy Quaid. It also features a fabulous score from legendary composer Hans Zimmer.

It’s been well over three decades since it hit cinemas but, in the wake of the success of the F1 movie (plus Cruise’s own legacy sequel triumph with Top Gun: Maverick), it certainly feels like the right time to get back on track.

Days of Thunder 2 is not the only sequel Cruise has on his plate, either; in April, 2026 Paramount confirmed the much-discussed sequel to Top Gun: Maverick was locked in and officially underway.

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

items.title: Don't Watch the Brilliantly Disgusting Clayface Trailer While You're Eating
items.description: DC Studios has released a new trailer for Clayface, and while it looks super cool, I wouldn’t recommend watching it while eating.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
DC Studios has released a new trailer for Clayface, and while it looks super cool, I wouldn’t recommend watching it while eating.

The trailer gives us our best look yet at Clayface, the next movie in James Gunn’s ongoing DC Universe. We get a good idea of the origin story for Matt Hagen / Clayface, who undergoes experimental treatment after he is left disfigured.

There are a number of standout moments in the trailer, but the one that’s stuck with me is when Hagen is forced to the restroom on a plane because his eyelids are melting together. He is so desperate to see that he looks like he’s about to cut his own eyelid skin. Ouch.

But there are plenty more disgusting moments of body horror, which is exactly how it should be for a movie of this kind. Directed by James Watkins from a screenplay by Mike Flanagan and Hossein Amini, Clayface is deliberately positioned as a counterpoint to the bright and breezy Superman and Supergirl films. It presents a nightmarish version of Peter Parker discovering his Spider-Man powers, except instead of sticking to walls and shooting out webs, Matt Hagen finds himself in the unfortunate position of coming to terms with his face falling off.

I will admit to the potential of some audience confusion with the release of Clayface, who is very much a Gotham-based Batman villain. The movie comes out before the recently delayed The Batman 2, which is not a part of Gunn’s DCU, rather Matt Reeves’ “Batman Epic Crime Saga.” So, don’t expect Robert Pattinson to pop out from the shadows in an end credit scene to temper Clayface's quest for revenge.

In fact, don’t expect Batman to show up at all — Gunn has yet to even announce who’s playing his Batman for the upcoming The Brave and the Bold movie, which will presumably take place in the Gotham we see in Clayface. Gunn has insisted he won’t start talking about it in any meaningful sense until The Batman 2 is out the door, and right now, that's February 18, 2028.

So, for now, Clayface is something of an oddity: a cool looking DCU standalone that may or may not have connections to the events we’ve already seen in Superman and Supergirl, and will see in next year’s Man of Tomorrow, and the DCU's future Batman. That’s fine by me, because if this trailer is anything to go by, Clayface has more than enough skin in the game.

Here's the official blurb on Clayface:

Matt Hagen’s meteoric rise from Gotham street kid to Hollywood leading man is tragically cut short when a local crime boss’s actions leave him horribly disfigured. Abandoned by his team and with nothing left, Matt seeks out a cutting edge treatment that miraculously returns him to his former self… but also unexpectedly affects his grip on reality, spiraling him down a destructive path of all-consuming revenge.

Clayface hits theaters in North America on October 23, 2026, and internationally beginning 21 October 2026.

items.title: Shenmue Fans Get Count Binface — a Man Dressed as a Trash Can Who's Going Up Against Nigel Farage in a UK Election — to Call on Sega to Make Shenmue 4
items.description: Count Binface has called on Sega to make Shenmue 4.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
What follows is a combination of words I never thought I’d write: Count Binface has called on Sega to make Shenmue 4.

Okay, this will need a bit of an explanation. Count Binface is a man who is famous in the UK for standing in local elections while wearing a trash can (we Brits call it a bin) on his head. He never wins; rather, his goal is to make the electoral process look ridiculous, and he's pretty good at it. Count Binface standing unceremoniously in the background while votes are read out for other candidates has a habit of making even the most sincere of politicians look more than a little silly.

But Count Binface is perhaps more famous now than he’s ever been, and that’s because he is the sole challenger to right-wing leader of the Reform UK party and Donald trump chum, Nigel Farage, who recently resigned as MP for Clacton, triggering a by-election in which he says he will stand. The resignation came amid allegations about his personal financing, which he continues to deny. Under increasing pressure, Farage took the high ground — or so he presumably thought — declaring that the “judges of my actions” should be his constituents.

Enter Count Binface, aka the comedian Jon Harvey, who confirmed he will run in the Clacton by-election. His slogan: “'My appeal is that I'm not Nigel Farage.”

This is an election showdown for the ages, and Count Binface might actually get some votes this time, because rival parties dismissed Farage’s actions as a stunt and said they would sit out the election. So, yes, we are set for Count Binface vs Nigel Farage, winner takes all (well, Clacton).

Okay. Still with me? Good. So, with Count Binface doing the rounds on super serious news programs on the BBC and the like, he’s carved out the time to issue a special message for Sega. Count Binface was commandeered by Shenmue fan group Shenmue Dojo, who used Cameo, a website where people pay celebrities for personalized video messages, to get Farage's political nemesis to issue a surprising call to action.

“Hi, Count Binface here, intergalactic space warrior and maybe the next MP for Clacton!" he says in the video.

“But, I have more important, pressing duties to do right now, because I need to say a galactic hello to Sega on behalf of the Shenmue fans. Now, I’m not just saying hello, Sega. I’ve got a little bone to pick with you because the fans would like to campaign for an update — from you, Sega — about Shenmue 4. Yes, they can’t leave you guys on another cliffhanger for years! Yes, I wonder whether Sega needs to be nationalized along with Adele?

“What do you say? Shall we harness the power of the Shenmue to ensure that there is no delay with updates ever again? I’d quite like the sound of that. I’d quite like to reboot SegaWorld in London’s Trocadero, and have old Sonic the Hedgehog back in his prime. Oh, that would be wonderful.

“But hey, I digress. The point is, the Shenmue fans are amazing. Sega, you need to get your bottoms in gear, sort yourselves out, get the update done.

“Whether you’re Sega or the Shenmue, the most important thing of course is to follow me. And when everyone comes to vote, make your votes Count!”

🚨 BREAKING: @CountBinface has cast his vote for Shenmue and now he has a message for @SEGA_OFFICIAL @SEGA .

The campaign continues. The people have spoken.#LetsGetShenmue4 pic.twitter.com/dnBhyTCdUz

— Shenmue Dojo 🥋 (@Shenmue_Dojo) July 20, 2026

I particularly like the drive-by request for the return of SegaWorld in Tracadero, which I used to frequent on occasion during my teen years to play arcade games. And Sonic returning to his prime? I imagine the bosses at Sega wouldn’t agree with that sentiment.

In fact, I’d love to be a fly on the wall when the people at the top of Sega catch wind of Count Binface’s video message, if they ever do. I suspect there would be more than a few confused faces.

As for Shenmue 4, despite the power of Count Binface, it remains an unlikely project. As of now, it's unknown if a fourth major Shenmue game will ever get made, though the franchise's fans certainly hope it happens. Shenmue creator Yu Suzuki told IGN in 2023 that he wanted to create a fourth game at some point. This, Suzuki hoped at the time, would win the game a warmer reception across a wider set of platforms, after a middling response to Shenmue 3 at the game's initial launch.

Honestly? It all sounds like rubbish to me.

Photo by Ryan Jenkinson/Getty Images.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: Star Trek Legend William Shatner and His Daughter Melanie Reveal They Battled Stage 4 Cancer at the Same Time
items.description: William Shatner and his daughter Melanie have said they battled stage 4 cancer at the same time.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
William Shatner and his daughter Melanie have said they battled stage 4 cancer at the same time.

People reported that the 95-year-old Star Trek legend, famous for playing Enterprise captain James T. Kirk, and his 61-year-old daughter Melanie supported each other through their joint cancer journeys, and are now cancer-free.

Melanie Shatner Gretsch received chemotherapy for stage 4 breast cancer. Meanwhile, In June 2023, William Shatner was diagnosed with stage 4 malignant melanoma that had spread to his lungs and brain. Shatner had surgery to remove the tumor on his face, then two years of immunotherapy for the cancer in his lungs and brain. In late 2024 both were declared cancer-free.

Both are now set to launch a podcast called No Time but Now, on which they interview health experts and other survivors. “I’m healthier now than I’ve been in years," Shatner said. "The brain is like a muscle. It feeds on activity."

It was recently revealed that the team behind current Star Trek show, Strange New Worlds, have tried to get Shatner himself back for a guest appearance ever since the series launched — despite the fact the last played the character when he was 60 years old, in 1994’s Star Trek Generations (the movie that killed Kirk off). The idea was that Shatner would play a version of Kirk who stayed in Depression-era New York with Joan Collins' Edith Keeler following the events of the episode The City on the Edge of Forever.

"I have been asked to come back as Kirk so many times. If Kirk is going to come back, it has to mean something,” Shatner said at a Vancouver convention in 2025, according to The Direct.

Photo by Barry King/WireImage.

items.title: Microsoft Announces Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC, With New Features and Achievements
items.description: Microsoft has announced Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC, allowing you to play classic console games on PC and handhelds such as the Xbox Ally X for the first time.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Microsoft has announced Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC, allowing you to play classic console games on PC and handhelds such as the Xbox Ally X for the first time.

The program begins today with an early preview, containing support for four titles: Blinx: The Time Sweeper, Conker: Live and Reloaded, Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge, and Fuzion Frenzy.

Anyone who owns the games already will automatically have a license granted on PC. The four games will also be added to Xbox Game Pass, for those with a PC Game Pass (or Ultimate) subscription. And, of course, you'll be able to stream the titles via Xbox Cloud Gaming, allowing you to play them on pretty much any rig.

Fresh features for Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC games include "up to 4x resolution upscaling, VSync support, Fullscreen and Windowed display modes, anisotropic filtering, enhanced anti-aliasing, and more," Xbox hardware architect Jason Ronald wrote in an announcement blog post. "These games also include customizable language and audio settings."

Finally, while unavailable today, Microsoft will add achievements to these games and future Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC titles via an update later this year.

"Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC is another step toward preserving the games from the past and making it easier for you to enjoy and play more of the games you already own across the devices you use every day," Ronald concluded.

Today's announcement feels like a much-needed piece of positivity after a bruising month for Xbox, following its devastating layoffs of 1,600 staff, and confirmation that another 1,600 will be let go over the course of this financial year. At least four studios have also been cut loose (Double Fine, Ninja Theory, Compulsion Games and Undead Labs), while the status of Blade maker Arkane remains unclear.

Rumors abound that Microsoft is set to continue its support for older games with the announcement of a disc-to-digital-license transferal program. A report earlier this month suggested that Project Helix, the next-generation Xbox, will not feature a disc drive. No further details were provided, but the news follows the bombshell dropped by PlayStation that it will no longer be producing or supporting physical game discs starting in January 2028. This suggests that the PlayStation 6 won't come with a disc drive, and that Sony is planning to embrace an all-digital future.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: [UPDATE] Stalker 2 Dev Hits Out at Founder's Comments on Xbox Exclusivity, Insist He Doesn't Know What He's Talking About
items.description: The founder of Stalker 2 developer GSC Game World has said the game turned a profit before it even came out thanks to the money Microsoft paid for Xbox exclusivity.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
UPDATE: GSC Game World has taken issue with founder Sergiy Grygorovych's recent comments about the money the company allegedly received for Stalker 2 Xbox exclusivity, insisting they "cannot be considered an accurate reflection of the actual state of affairs."

In a statement issued to IGN, GSC Game World said the company's owner, Max Krippa, funded the majority of the development budget. GSC Game World did not detail the nature of the company's deal with Microsoft for exclusivity, how much money it received as part of the deal, nor confirm Stalker 2's development budget.

Here's the statement in full:

GSC Game World refrained from commenting for a long time on Sergiy Grygorovych's public statements about the company. However, we now consider it necessary to respond, as continued silence may be perceived as confirmation of information that is simply not true.

In particular, his recent claims, including his statements regarding the relationship between S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 and the Xbox teams, do not reflect the actual facts.

In accordance with the agreements reached between the parties, Sergiy was not involved either in negotiations with partners regarding S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 or in the actual development of the game throughout its full production cycle. We have always fully honored these agreements on our side. For this reason, his comments regarding the company's activities cannot be considered an accurate reflection of the actual state of affairs.

The development of S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 became one of the most challenging projects in the history of the video game industry. We believe the story of this game should be based on facts, not on assumptions or subjective opinions.

We are sincerely grateful to everyone who made the game's release possible: the defenders of Ukraine, our players, our partners, and, of course, the company's owner, Max Krippa, who funded the majority of the development budget.

We hope that such public statements will not distract attention from what truly matters to the team today. GSC Game World is currently putting the finishing touches on a significant update for S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2, as well as its first large-scale story DLC. We will be sharing more details very soon.

ORIGINAL STORY: The founder of Stalker 2 developer GSC Game World has said the game turned a profit before it even came out thanks to the money Microsoft paid for Xbox exclusivity.

In an interview with YouTuber OLDboi, GSC Game World founder Sergiy Grygorovych said that Microsoft was so impressed by the number of views the debut Stalker 2 trailer received, that it soon got in touch with the Ukraine company to negotiate terms for exclusivity.

“We took more than the cost of Stalker 2,” Grygorovych, who has since left GSC Game World to make a new game with a new studio, said. “It paid for itself before the first day.” IGN has asked GSC Game World for comment.

Xbox was heavily involved with Stalker 2, which was made amid Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. It snapped up timed console exclusivity and a day-one launch on Xbox Game Pass, while also helping to produce and market the game, as well as a making-of documentary.

After a series of understandable delays, Stalker 2 launched on PC and Xbox Series X and S in November 2024, as well as on Game Pass. It was released on PlayStation 5 a year later, in November 2025. Stalker 2 was originally due out much earlier, in Q4 2021, as per documents revealed in 2021.

Stalker 2 was a sales success, hitting 1 million copies in two days. It has so far surpassed 6 million players. Cost of Hope, the first major story expansion for Stalker 2, launched in the summer.

Grygorovych did not say how much money Microsoft paid for the exclusivity, nor how much Stalker 2 cost to develop. But his comments do shine a light on Microsoft’s gaming philosophy when it was building up its content portfolio to help boost interest in Game Pass.

Indeed, developers have over the years praised Microsoft for cutting generous deals for Game Pass and exclusivity, with some saying they helped reduce risk and keep studios afloat.

Now, amid new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s “reset” of Microsoft’s gaming business, the future of Game Pass is unclear. Microsoft cut 1,600 staff from Xbox earlier this month, with another 1,600 to go this financial year. Sharma has pulled Call of Duty out of Game Pass as a day-one launch title, and is doubling down on Xbox’s biggest franchises, such as Fallout. Four studios are confirmed to be leaving Microsoft ownership, with another on its way. Sharma has called it the most “significant” restructure in Xbox history, insisting Microsoft’s gaming business “is not healthy.”

Speaking on MinnMax, Mike Brown, who was creative director on the hugely successful Forza Horizon 5 before leaving developer Playground to found his own studio, Maverick Games, which is set to release an open world racer of his own called Clutch, said this week that Game Pass had failed to hit enough subscribers to justify Microsoft’s huge spending on content acquisition. This includes the eye-watering $69 billion Microsoft splashed out on Call of Duty developer Activision Blizzard.

“I think it's really sad and I think it's really, really unfortunate,” Brown began. “They've honestly invested a fortune in the concept of Game Pass as a service, which led to loads of teams being acquired, loads of games being funded, loads of people getting jobs, all with a vision of getting regular games landing in this service for players. I think the reality is not enough people have subscribed to it at the prices that they needed to pay in order to make that business viable.

“And, that’s actually just really sad. Because we're now going to see studios getting shut down or spun off, and loads of people are going to lose their jobs, and that is honestly just a result of a well-meaning, player-focused concept of Xbox Game Pass not quite landing.”

Brown went on to defend Microsoft and Game Pass, praising the concept of the subscription service and the games that would otherwise not have been made were it not to have existed.

“It’s just a real shame,” he continued. “And as much as people point fingers and call different people within Xbox the villain of the piece, the concept of Game Pass was good. Like, it's a good idea. Let's have a subscription, make it affordable, try and get games to more people. We'll have a really diverse selection of games on there. We'll get a load of studios involved. For this reason, his comments regarding the company's activities cannot be considered an accurate reflection of the actual state of affairs.

The development of S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 became one of the most challenging projects in the history of the video game industry. We believe the story of this game should be based on facts, not on assumptions or subjective opinions.

We are sincerely grateful to everyone who made the game's release possible: the defenders of Ukraine, our players, our partners, and, of course, the company's owner, Max Krippa, who funded the majority of the development budget.

We hope that such public statements will not distract attention from what truly matters to the team today. GSC Game World is currently putting the finishing touches on a significant update for S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2, as well as its first large-scale story DLC. We will be sharing more details very soon.

items.title: Kevin Feige Says Marvel Has Movies Planned 'All the Way Up to 2042,' Including a Major X-Men Push and Live-Action Miles Morales
items.description: Marvel has mapped out its movie plans up to 2042, studio boss Kevin Feige has said, hinting at a "streamlined, simplified" universe post-Avengers: Secret Wars, a big push for the new X-Men, and plans to eventually unveil a live-action Miles Morales.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Marvel has mapped out its movie plans up to 2042, studio boss Kevin Feige has said, hinting at a "streamlined, simplified" universe post-Avengers: Secret Wars, a big push for the new X-Men, and plans to eventually unveil a live-action Miles Morales.

Speaking to Chinese outlet Watching Hollywood during a recent tour of Shanghai, Feige described this year's Avengers: Doomsday and next year's Avengers: Secret Wars as a conclusion to storylines that started before the MCU itself (such as the fates of some original X-Men). At the same time, Feige also contrasted Secret Wars with the climactic Avengers: Endgame, suggesting that 2027's blockbuster would act as a new beginning for the franchise, as well as a conclusion of the Multiverse saga.

"We want to do two things," Feige began (via machine translation). "First, to bring some storylines to a close, those that started long before Iron Man, including the original X-Men characters. Second, to simultaneously set the stage for the future.

"Avengers: Endgame was truly an end, and since then, we've tried and experimented with many new things. But [Secret Wars] is a beginning. It will establish a streamlined, simplified, single universe that audiences can keep up with. Some things will be familiar, but many, many things will be entirely new."

Feige said that the new don't-call-it-a-reboot post-Secret Wars MCU will hopefully attract a "new generation of audiences" to Marvel, something that tallies with past comments by Feige that, one day, the franchise will eventually bring in new versions of existing heroes such as Iron Man. For now, though, Marvel seems to have one major brand in mind to lead the next saga: the X-Men.

"Fundamentally, the X-Men will be at its core," Feige said. "Acquiring the X-Men rights isn't just about... for example, Wolverine is an outstanding character, and we were able to team him up with Deadpool, which is great. But the X-Men are far more than just Wolverine, far more than the original team; fundamentally, it's a universe, a multi-stage saga. Much of that is what we're working towards."

In other words, don't expect Jake Schreier's upcoming X-Men movie to be a one-and-done affair (although, honestly, this always seemed a remote possibility). Instead, the X-Men sound like they'll form the bedrock of Marvel's storytelling in the post-Secret Wars era, which seems fitting, since the next phase will be known as the Mutant Saga.

"We were just in a Marvel Studios meeting room, planning movies all the way up to 2042," Feige revealed. "Whether we can make it to 2042? Who knows? Will it be those movies? Who knows? But this is how we approach and plan the vast amount of potential stories in the comics. We're constantly changing, constantly evolving, but having some guidance helps us act more purposefully… especially with X-Men — it's already had 10 movies, some very, very good, some I think haven't lived up to expectations — how do we plan the Mutant Saga in a very grand way?"

Marvel is set to make a splash at this weekend's San Diego Comic-Con, returning to Hall H for the first time in two years ahead of this month's hugely-anticipated Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and this December's Avengers: Doomsday. Fans are hoping that, alongside more details on both of those, Feige will lift the lid on more of Marvel's future roadmap — maybe not up until 2042, but at least for the next few years.

Currently, Marvel has not officially announced a launch plan for anything beyond December 2027's Avengers: Secret Wars, though it has acknowledged that its X-Men reboot and Black Panther 3 are in the planning stages. Other projects waiting in the wings include a long-gestating Nova project (now retooled as a movie rather than a Disney+ series), and an ambition to eventually make a Shang-Chi 2.

What else could be on Marvel's roadmap, leading up to 2042? While many classic characters feel like they've run their course (it would be a surprise to see Captain America, Ant-Man or Captain Marvel get further standalone films after the financial performance of Brave New World, Quantumania and The Marvels), others still feel like they have some gas left in the tank.

It would not be a surprise to see Marvel eventually make a Doctor Strange 3, or a Thor 5. I could also see Marvel taking another chance on the Fantastic Four, even if their first outing felt a little underwhelming. And then there's the hugely popular character of Wanda Maximoff, whose eventual return feels inevitable. Could we finally get a solo Scarlet Witch movie?

Most obvious, of course, is more Spider-Man. Sony and Marvel are clearly keen, and Tom Holland has hinted he expects to return for at least one more Spider-Man film, with plans to eventually hand over his webbing capsules to a younger replacement. Holland recently suggested he would be keen to pass the baton to a live-action Miles Morales — and clearly, this is a character on Feige's radar, too.

"One of the fun things about this business is that we're always dreaming and coming up with ideas," Feige said when asked about the character. "There's a line in Spider-Man: No Way Home where Electro says, 'Somewhere there's bound to be a black Spider-Man.' Audiences around the world were thrilled because they knew it might be a hint at Miles.

"The good news is, Sony has the Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse series, which are very popular and excellent, and Beyond the Universe is coming out next year. But yes, we definitely have plans, and I think a live-action Spider-Man movie has this destiny: to add Miles sometime after the Spider-Verse series ends. We've been thinking and discussing more Spider-Man adventures, regardless of agreements or contracts. My production partner, Amy Pascal, is already working on it, and we've had in-depth discussions about what the next two, three, four, and five Spider-Man movies might be about."

See you in 2042 for Spider-Man 9, then? In the meantime, be sure to keep an eye on IGN this weekend for everything from Marvel at SDCC, including all of the big announcements from Hall H as they happen.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: How Luke and Anakin's Missing Hands Reshaped Kylo Ren's Lightsaber - Exclusive
items.description: Star Wars: The Force Awakens 3D modeling supervisor Jet Cooper exclusively reveals how Luke Skywalker and Darth Vader’s severed hands directly inspired the design of Kylo Ren’s crossguard lightsaber.
items.author: Michael Peyton
items.content:
Nearly 12 years ago, we got our very first glimpse at the new big Star Wars villain — Kylo Ren, aka Ben Solo, the grandson of Darth Vader — in what would become one of the highest-grossing movies of all time. Smack dab in the middle of the first teaser for Star Wars: The Force Awakens, Ren lumbers through a snowy planet and fires up his red lightsaber. A second later – in a moment in which the internet would lose its collective mind – he switched on the crossguard of his saber, a big screen first.

While the exact design of Kylo Ren’s lightsaber has been canonically explained, many of the secrets about its creation have been under wraps – until now. Jet Cooper, the 3D Modelling Supervisor of Star Wars: The Force Awakens, says that both Luke Skywalker and Darth Vader’s sliced-off hands directly led to the inclusion of the crossguard on Kylo Ren’s saber. I spoke with Cooper exclusively about the many decisions that went into crafting the iconic weapon and how much changed between the initial design and on-screen product.

The lightsaber had gone through various iterations throughout the design process. Cooper and The Force Awakens director and producer J.J. Abrams dug back centuries, looking at knights’ swords, for inspiration.

“The original [version] was in a saber shape without a flare on the end of it,” Cooper says, “because Kylo Ren was very much a knight but really, really crude. We’d suggested casually in a conversation one day that everyone was losing their hands. Luke lost his hand. Vader lost his hand. And the reason Europeans put quillons on swords was to stop that from happening.

“[Ren’s saber has] the main beam with the cracked crystal, so it's really irregular. But what happens if we split that beam and divert it at the sides? Then, of course, Europeans used that part of the sword like a weapon, like a blade. It was nice that J.J. had Kylo Ren turn that and then push [the guard] into the person up against a tree. So, basically it's an old-fashioned broad sword.”

While the weapon has roots in European history, Cooper says he and Abrams had another rationale for changing up Kylo’s lightsaber design.

“[Another] reason we flared the end out was so that, when you have a silhouette of it, that a 12-year-old could tell what it was.”

Cooper, who also worked on movies like Skyfall, X-Men: First Class, and Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom, says that Kylo Ren’s lightsaber is among the creations he’s most proud of.

“My favorite thing I've got in my office that I always do a show-and-tell with is Kylo Ren's lightsaber,” Cooper says. “I got to design that with J.J. Abrams and [we] finished on version number 13. Lucky number 13.”

In addition to making props for blockbuster movies, Cooper serves as Creative Director and Head of 3D at Makinarium – who just unveiled a one-of-a-kind Terminator collectible that’s available to preorder now. While he’s had a long career in the movie business working on massive franchises and smaller movies alike, much of Cooper’s love of prop making traces back to a galaxy far, far away.

“When I was 8 years old, I saw the original Star Wars,” Cooper says. “I came out of the theater thinking ‘That's what I want to do when I grow up!’ It’s magic.”

Michael Peyton is the Senior Editorial Director of Events & Entertainment at IGN, leading entertainment content and coverage of tentpole events including IGN Live, San Diego Comic Con, gamescom, and IGN Fan Fest. He's spent 20 years working in the games and entertainment industry, and his adventures have taken him everywhere from the Oscars to Japan to Buenos Aires, Argentina. Follow him on Bluesky @MichaelPeyton

items.title: Avengers: Doomsday Trailer Has Some Fans Saying Marvel Should Have Built Up Towards Doctor Doom's Appearance Like It Did for Thanos — but There's a Clear Counterpoint
items.description: The Avengers: Doomsday trailer has some fans saying Marvel should have built up towards Doctor Doom's appearance like it did for Thanos — but there's a clear counterpoint.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
As the dust settles on the Avengers: Doomsday trailer, I’ve seen a mixed reception emerge. There’s plenty of excitement about the first Avengers movie since 2019’s all-conquering Endgame, and much fun speculation about the true nature of Steve Rogers' appearance. Clearly, the mainstream audience is on board, too, with impressive day-one advance ticket sales and huge views for the trailer itself.

But tempering the excitement somewhat are complaints not just around the visual effects we see in the trailer, or a perceived reinforcement of MCU fatigue some say they feel while watching the trailer, but Doctor Doom’s star turn as the villain.

My timeline is full of people saying that the introduction of Doctor Doom feels rushed, that it should have been built up over the course of multiple movies for fans to feel the excitement of a pay off much like the one they got when the Avengers teamed up to battle Thanos. Thanos, let's remember, appeared in cameo form in 2014’s Guardians of the Galaxy and 2015’s Avengers: Age of Ultron before starring in 2018's Infinity War and finally biting the dust in Endgame. Indeed, Thanos first reared his ugly head all the way back in 2012’s The Avengers.

Doctor Doom, played by Iron Man actor Robert Downey Jr., however, has had little to no build up. Yes, he appeared, menacingly, at the end of last year’s The Fantastic Four: First Steps with Reed Richards and Sue Storm’s son, Franklin (we’re still not sure what Doom wants with him). But that’s it, which leaves us with a debut appearance in this December’s Avengers: Doomsday.

This, some say, is evidence of Marvel Studios’ rushed attempt to create a big bad for its cinematic universe after the plan for Kang fell apart. Doom is the MCU's Hail Mary, a last-ditch attempt to rekindle the glory days amid waning interest in superheroes. But, others counter, there is hope amid the doom and gloom.

Let us consider the many, many wonderful villains who have graced our screens without any build up at all. Darth Vader didn’t need a handful of cameo appearances before be became perhaps the greatest villain of all time in A New Hope. I don’t remember Hannibal Lecter making weird noises from the shadows in movies set before The Silence of the Lambs. Nor did Sauron require the hours and hours of origin story we have subsequently received for The Fellowship of the Ring’s journey to Mordor to hit hard.

Perhaps the best example of a successful villain who needed little introduction came from the MCU itself. I’ve always thought of Ultron as the standout character in the otherwise disappointing Avengers: Age of Ultron. This was a villain who wasn’t just introduced and defeated all in one movie, but created.

So, it’s perfectly reasonable to expect a successful introduction of Doctor Doom in Avengers: Doomsday, which I'm sure will be long enough to accommodate plenty of exposition. It will, as most things in movies do, come down to the story, the characters, the direction, and of course the performances of the actors. I don’t need a build up to Doom’s reveal for Robert Downey Jr.'s inevitable 'how can you have Tony Stark’s face?' conversation with Thor and Captain America to get my heart racing. To dismiss Doomsday now because we haven’t had a few Doom teases beforehand seems a little premature.

In any case, Doomsday might be the Doom setup. While he's the main event in the Doomsday trailer, we may not see much of the character in the movie itself. Rather, the big fights and Doom debates may be reserved for next year's Secret Wars. We might not even see Doom take off his mask in Doomsday, or any other character see his face.

While we wait to find out how this Doom thing is going to go, we’ve got plenty more on Avengers: Doomsday to digest. For example, there's a debate about whether a character was edited out of one shot from the trailer. Is it Doctor Doom? Speaking of Doom, we also have a new Avengers: Doomsday poster that teases Doctor Doom's motivation in the story.

Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters December 18, 2026. Here's the official synopsis:

As the dust settles on the Avengers: Doomsday trailer, I’ve seen a mixed reception emerge. There’s plenty of excitement about the first Avengers movie since 2019’s all-conquering Endgame, and much fun speculation about the true nature of Steve Rogers' appearance. Clearly, the mainstream audience is on board, too, with impressive day-one advance ticket sales and huge views for the trailer itself.

But tempering the excitement somewhat are complaints not just around the visual effects we see in the trailer, or a perceived reinforcement of MCU fatigue some say they feel while watching the trailer, but Doctor Doom’s star turn as the villain.

My timeline is full of people saying that the introduction of Doctor Doom feels rushed, that it should have been built up over the course of multiple movies for fans to feel the excitement of a pay off much like the one they got when the Avengers teamed up to battle Thanos. Thanos, let's remember, appeared in cameo form in 2014’s Guardians of the Galaxy and 2015’s Avengers: Age of Ultron before starring in 2018's Infinity War and finally biting the dust in Endgame. Indeed, Thanos first reared his ugly head all the way back in 2012’s The Avengers.

Doctor Doom, played by Iron Man actor Robert Downey Jr., however, has had little to no build up. Yes, he appeared, menacingly, at the end of last year’s The Fantastic Four: First Steps with Reed Richards and Sue Storm’s son, Franklin (we’re still not sure what Doom wants with him). But that’s it, which leaves us with a debut appearance in this December’s Avengers: Doomsday.

This, some say, is evidence of Marvel Studios’ rushed attempt to create a big bad for its cinematic universe after the plan for Kang fell apart. Doom is the MCU's Hail Mary, a last-ditch attempt to rekindle the glory days amid waning interest in superheroes. But, others counter, there is hope amid the doom and gloom.

Let us consider the many, many wonderful villains who have graced our screens without any build up at all. Darth Vader didn’t need a handful of cameo appearances before be became perhaps the greatest villain of all time in A New Hope. I don’t remember Hannibal Lecter making weird noises from the shadows in movies set before The Silence of the Lambs. Nor did Sauron require the hours and hours of origin story we have subsequently received for The Fellowship of the Ring’s journey to Mordor to hit hard.

Perhaps the best example of a successful villain who needed little introduction came from the MCU itself. I’ve always thought of Ultron as the standout character in the otherwise disappointing Avengers: Age of Ultron. This was a villain who wasn’t just introduced and defeated all in one movie, but created.

So, it’s perfectly reasonable to expect a successful introduction of Doctor Doom in Avengers: Doomsday, which I'm sure will be long enough to accommodate plenty of exposition. It will, as most things in movies do, come down to the story, the characters, the direction, and of course the performances of the actors. I don’t need a build up to Doom’s reveal for Robert Downey Jr.'s inevitable 'how can you have Tony Stark’s face?' conversation with Thor and Captain America to get my heart racing. To dismiss Doomsday now because we haven’t had a few Doom teases beforehand seems a little premature.

In any case, Doomsday might be the Doom setup. While he's the main event in the Doomsday trailer, we may not see much of the character in the movie itself. Rather, the big fights and Doom debates may be reserved for next year's Secret Wars. We might not even see Doom take off his mask in Doomsday, or any other character see his face.

items.title: Black Lake Horror Game Announced for PC
items.description: First-person horror games are some of our favorite kind, as they bring the scary stuff right in front of your character's eyes. In Black Lake, developer Polydin Studio ups that ante by setting this spooky psychological/survival horror game not just in an abandoned orphanage in search of your missing twin sister, but one that's abandoned and floating at sea. It's in development for PC and consoles.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
First-person horror games are some of our favorite kind, as they bring the scary stuff right in front of your character's eyes. In Black Lake, developer Polydin Studio ups that ante by setting this spooky psychological/survival horror game not just in an abandoned orphanage in search of your missing twin sister, but one that's abandoned and floating at sea. It's in development for PC and consoles, with the PC version due out in Winter 2027 and the console versions expected to follow in mid-2027. Check out the first trailer above and the first screenshots in the gallery below.

Polydin describes the story setup as follows: "You play as Elena, who returns to the place where she grew up after receiving a message from her missing twin sister, Rita. The orphanage should have been empty. Instead, its halls are still warm, the bells are ringing again, and something has been moving through the walls. As Elena follows Rita’s trail, she uncovers the remains of a forbidden ritual tied to the children who vanished from the orphanage years ago. Some of them may still be here, though not in any form she remembers."

You'll utilize tools like your phone, candles, and lantern to stay alive, with light being particularly crucial. The developers note that "some creatures fear the scent of burning wax," so have fun with that one! You'll encounter plenty of puzzles along the way that are centered around rituals, utilizing objects in the environment. The endless black ocean surrounds you, your weapons will be limited, and in a particularly terrifying twist, Polydin says you'll need to "hide, distract, evade, and survive terrifying creatures formed from the orphanage’s missing children and staff." Peachy!

You can wishlist Black Lake on Steam if you're interested.
